company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS with $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the quality was low — the upside was driven by tariff refunds (145 basis point tailwind to gross margins) and a non-cash LIFO benefit (105 basis point tailwind) rather than organic strength. Domestic comps disappointed at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence in fiscal 2027 sales growth.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth, making it a meaningful strategic bet on the robotics and Physical AI buildout.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, putting clean EPS at 42 cents. Sales were a miss, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS band of $1.85–2.15 was held unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International, signaling a seasoned appointment.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% estimate, as management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure squeezing consumers. Revenue of $2.311 billion came in above the Street's $2.17 billion but the margin story dominated. Bright spots include healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a ~75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog year-over-year, though no formal fiscal 2027 guidance was provided.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, which showed 22% weight loss — a highly competitive result in the increasingly crowded obesity drug space. The data meaningfully de-risks the program and reinforces Viking as a credible GLP-1 challenger.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector faces headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation are pressuring consumer budgets and keeping retail soft. Robotics and Physical AI theme gets a boost from the Cognex/RealSense deal. GLP-1/obesity drug space remains highly active with Viking's strong VK2735 data.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This edition is a focused company-specific earnings note with no broad macro or index commentary, so let's get straight into the names moving this morning.

Starting with Viking Therapeutics — shares are spiking hard in the pre-market after the company reported a 22% weight loss result from its GLP-1 drug VK2735 in clinical trials. That is a highly competitive number in the obesity drug space and meaningfully de-risks the program. Viking is increasingly a name the big players have to take seriously.

Over at AutoZone, the company beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03 — but the quality of that beat is the problem. The upside came almost entirely from tariff refunds, a 145 basis point gross margin tailwind, and a non-cash LIFO benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is much less impressive. Domestic comps grew only 1.6% versus the Street's 3.1% expectation, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did say sales improved in the final eight weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence in fiscal 2027 growth, but this is a low-quality beat.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotics and Physical AI — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus another 106 million dollars. RealSense is expected to generate 80 to 90 million dollars in revenue, which represents more than 50% year-over-year growth. This is a direct play on the robotics buildout and positions Cognex more aggressively in the Physical AI theme.

MillerKnoll had a solid quarter — earnings per share of 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents, and importantly they would have beaten even without the tariff refund tailwind. Clean earnings per share was 42 cents, still well above the 36-cent consensus. Sales were light at $923 million versus $943 million expected, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year revenue guidance was trimmed slightly while the earnings per share band was held unchanged — call it a mixed but net-positive report.

THOR Industries missed on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — 78 cents versus 87 cents expected — with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%. Management's commentary was candid and cautious, pointing to stubborn interest rates, high fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets. No formal fiscal 2027 guidance was provided. That said, dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost cuts are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year — so there are green shoots buried in an otherwise weak print.

Finally, Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November first. Hau has a strong track record with prior CFO roles at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International — a credible hire.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the high-momentum name to watch on the GLP-1 data. Cognex gets a strategic boost from the RealSense deal. AutoZone and THOR are the disappointments. Stay focused, manage size, and good luck out there.
